analysis:
Only base_text for docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 1-860) was supplied. There is no patch or head text, so the actual PR change is not visible and no new regression can be attributed to it. Coverage limit: the diff and any other changed files were not seen.

Security-relevant base content to check against the head side:
- Logout (lines 431-480): sends the saved token as a Bearer credential to the issuer recorded in auth_token.issuer.json (A-008). It follows no redirects and has a 10s timeout, and only HTTP 204 confirms revocation. The request keeps the original coordinator host and port. Legacy credentials without issuer metadata get local deletion with remote revocation unconfirmed. The credential-holding process is stopped and its lock and lease are held through revocation. Related: T-053.
- Cache commands (lines 18-40): cache set --directory pins a volume UUID, and invalid or changed storage disables the SSD cache. Docs state the checks do not certify disk firmware (T-041, SEC-035). Daily write limit and TTL claims should stay consistent with the 30-minute sliding TTL.
- Enroll and App Attest (lines 548-562): macOS 27+ returns guidance only, grants no authorization, and keeps legacy enrollment for frozen identities (TB-011, T-052, T-054, T-057).
- Other: macOS upgrade notice performs no network or config operations. The hidden native-serve-qualification entry requires an env var, literal 127.0.0.1 and owner-only inputs. Models switch and replace, and local endpoint --no-auth, are documented.

If the head side changes any of these claims, such as the token-revocation guarantees, App Attest authorization semantics, or cache TTL and storage guarantees, check it against TB-011, T-053 and T-041.
